title: Matrix Optimization via Column Inversions
description:
Given a binary matrix of size m x n, you are permitted to perform any number of column flips. A flip on a column involves changing all 0s to 1s and all 1s to 0s within that specific column.

Your objective is to determine the maximum number of rows that can be made identical after an optimal sequence of column flips. A set of rows is identical if every cell in a row contains the same value (either all 0s or all 1s).

Hint: Two rows can be made to consist of the same value if they are initially identical or if one is the bitwise complement of the other.
input_format:
The first line contains two integers m and n, representing the number of rows and columns.
The next m lines each contain n space-separated integers (0 or 1), representing the binary matrix.
output_format: Print a single integer representing the maximum number of rows that can be made identical.
constraints:
1 <= m, n <= 300
Each cell is either 0 or 1
